correctness.rationale: A vertex subset is P3-convex exactly when every unselected vertex has at most one selected neighbor. For rooted trees t>=5, A(H,v)>=2t−2 by leaf removal and two additional sets; for nonstar trees m>=6, one-neighbor defect D(T,v)>=2m−4 via path subsets and disconnected pairs. Adding a leaf yields c(T+)=2c(T)−D(T,v). Exact broom counts c(B_n)=3·2^(n−3)+2n−2 and strict nonhub defects for m>=9 give equality rigidity. Independently generated all 47 unlabeled n=9 tree types using canonical rooted parentheses, directly counted valid subsets and confirmed unique broom maximum 208; induction establishes all n>=9 trees. Additional edges strictly remove at least one convex set; universal-vertex nonstars bounded by star plus leaf-edge, extending to all connected simple nonstars. Finite n=9 enumeration supplies only induction base, not an infinite proof.
